title: ThreadsIPadView
description: Create AggregatorApp/iPad/Threads/ThreadsIPadView.swift. Landscape: content column shows thread list — reuse existing ThreadsViewModel and ThreadRowView if the audit confirmed reusability; selection sets iPadNavigationModel.selectedThread; detail column renders ThreadDetailView / ArticleDetailView driven by selectedThread. Portrait: thread list in the detail column; tapping pushes thread detail within the detail column's implicit NavigationStack. Handle Empty, Loading, and Error states explicitly.
acceptance_criteria: Landscape: thread list in content column, detail view in detail column driven by selection
Portrait: thread list in detail column, tap pushes thread detail
Empty, Loading, and Error states are explicitly rendered
Existing Threads views are not modified
Reuses ThreadsViewModel without modification if audit confirmed reusable

handoff_summary.completed: Created ThreadsIPadView.swift with: Loading/Empty/Error/Loaded state handling; landscape mode where thread rows are Buttons that set iPadNavigationModel.selectedThread with accent-color selection highlight; portrait mode where the view wraps itself in a NavigationStack and rows use NavigationLink(value: thread.id) pushing ThreadDetailView; cursor-based pagination; pull-to-refresh; dismiss/restore swipe actions; sort/filter toolbar menu. Fixed pre-existing SidebarView.swift build error (List selection overload unavailable on iOS — fixed with Binding<AppSection?> wrapper).
handoff_summary.remaining: AppRootIPad.swift still shows placeholder Text("Section List") and Text("Detail") — a downstream bead must wire ThreadsIPadView into the content column and ThreadDetailView (driven by iPadNavigationModel.selectedThread) into the detail column. UIScreen.main deprecation warnings in TodayIPadView.swift are pre-existing and outside this bead's scope.
handoff_summary.risks: ThreadsIPadView is not yet wired into AppRootIPad — it will not appear until AppRootIPad is updated. The UIScreen.main orientation approach produces deprecation warnings on iOS 26; a future bead should migrate to windowScene screen bounds. No iPhone views were modified.
handoff_summary.next_action: Wire ThreadsIPadView into AppRootIPad content column (landscape) and detail column (portrait), and show ThreadDetailView in AppRootIPad's detail column driven by iPadNavigationModel.selectedThread.
handoff_summary.conflict_risks: AppRootIPad.swift still has placeholder content — the sibling bead that wires AppRootIPad must import ThreadsIPadView into the content column. No file-level conflicts expected since AppRootIPad was not modified here.
handoff_summary.design_decisions: 1. No separate ViewModel: ThreadsView has no extracted ViewModel (all state is in the view), so ThreadsIPadView duplicates the loading/pagination logic inline — the same pattern as the iPhone view. 2. Orientation detection via UIDevice.orientationDidChangeNotification + UIScreen.main.bounds ratio, matching AppRootIPad's existing approach. 3. Portrait NavigationStack wraps the full list body so ThreadDetailView's own NavigationLinks (to ArticleDetailView) continue to work within the stack. 4. Landscape selection highlight: accentColor.opacity(0.12) background on the selected row gives a visual affordance without a native List selection binding (which would require AppSection? pattern). 5. Toolbar uses explicit Binding(get:set:) to avoid @Bindable inside @ToolbarContentBuilder — more predictable across SwiftUI versions. 6. SidebarView fix: List(_:selection:rowContent:) with non-optional Binding<AppSection> is unavailable on iOS; wrapped with Binding<AppSection?> adapter — minimal, non-breaking change.
handoff_summary.test_coverage_notes: Tester should verify: (a) loading spinner appears before first fetch, (b) empty state shows ContentUnavailableView with correct SF Symbol, (c) error state shows localizedDescription and Retry button, (d) thread list renders ThreadCardView rows, (e) in landscape tapping a row sets iPadNavigationModel.selectedThread and highlights the row, (f) in portrait tapping a row pushes ThreadDetailView within the embedded NavigationStack, (g) pull-to-refresh clears and reloads, (h) swipe to dismiss removes the row and calls the API, (i) sort and showDismissed toggles reload the list, (j) scrolling to last row triggers loadNextPage. iPhone views must be unaffected.
handoff_summary.known_limitations: 1. ThreadsIPadView is not yet displayed — AppRootIPad still shows placeholder text and must be updated to route the .threads section to this view. 2. Landscape detail column is not managed by this view; AppRootIPad must show ThreadDetailView driven by navigationModel.selectedThread. 3. UIScreen.main.bounds is deprecated on iOS 26 — produces warnings; a future bead should replace with windowScene screen bounds. 4. Portrait initial isPortrait state defaults to false (landscape) and is corrected on .onAppear — this may briefly show the wrong layout if the view appears before onAppear fires, but this is imperceptible in practice.

conflict_risks: AppRootIPad.swift still has placeholder content — the sibling bead that wires AppRootIPad must import ThreadsIPadView into the content column. No file-level conflicts expected since AppRootIPad was not modified here.

execution_history.summary: Created AggregatorApp/iPad/Threads/ThreadsIPadView.swift with full landscape (content-column list → iPadNavigationModel.selectedThread) and portrait (NavigationStack push) behavior. Also fixed a pre-existing compile error in SidebarView.swift (List selection API required Binding<AppSection?> not Binding<AppSection> on iOS). Build succeeds with exit code 0.

# Developer Guardrails

Primary responsibility: Implement only the assigned bead inside the existing architecture and file scope.

## Corrective bead scope

If your `bead_id` ends in `-corrective` or `-corrective-<N>` (e.g. `B-abc12345-corrective`, `B-abc12345-test-corrective-2`), you are running as a CORRECTIVE bead. Your scope is **strictly limited to fixing the specific failure that blocked the parent bead**. Do not:

- Add unrelated improvements, refactors, or cleanup, even if you notice them
- Reapply previously-reverted changes (the operator reverted them for a reason)
- Expand the surface area beyond what is needed to unblock the parent
- Touch files outside what the parent bead's `expected_files` / `expected_globs` covered, unless the failure is genuinely in another file and there is no smaller fix

If you notice an unrelated issue while fixing the corrective scope: **file a separate bead** via `takt bead create` describing what you saw, but do not fix it in this corrective. The operator will prioritize and dispatch.

When in doubt about scope: prefer the smallest possible fix. The reviewer of this corrective will check that the scope was respected.

Allowed actions:
- Modify code, configuration, or local docs required to complete the assigned bead.
- Create sub-beads for discovered follow-up work that should be handled separately.
- Verify your `Swift` changes compile and import correctly with a quick syntax check: ``.

Disallowed actions:
- Run any test suite — not even a targeted `` run or any subset. Test execution is exclusively the tester agent's responsibility. Running tests wastes the agent budget and delays the pipeline.
- Redesign unrelated architecture or broaden scope beyond the assigned bead.
- Perform final review signoff in place of a review agent.
- Silently absorb unrelated test, documentation, or planning work that should be handed off.

## Memory

**Read memory at bead start.** Before touching any code, run three searches using `$TAKT_CMD` (injected by the orchestrator):

```bash
$TAKT_CMD memory search "<bead topic keywords>" --namespace global
$TAKT_CMD memory search "<bead topic keywords>" --namespace feature:<feature_root_id>
$TAKT_CMD memory search "<bead topic keywords>" --namespace specs
```

Treat results as ambient context — apply relevant entries; skip entries that don't apply.

**Write to memory when you discover reusable project knowledge** — something that would have changed your approach if you had known it upfront, and is not already in CLAUDE.md or the guardrails.

```bash
$TAKT_CMD memory add "<concise fact>" --namespace global               # project-wide knowledge
$TAKT_CMD memory add "<discovery>" --namespace feature:<feature_root_id>  # feature-scoped
```

Required Handoff Fields:

Every developer bead **must** populate the following three fields in its output JSON. Reviewers and tester agents rely on these fields to scope their work without additional back-and-forth turns. Use `"N/A"` only when a field is genuinely inapplicable (e.g., a trivial rename with no design trade-offs); do not leave fields blank.

- **`design_decisions`** — Document non-obvious architectural or implementation choices made during this bead. Include alternatives considered and why the chosen approach was preferred. Reviewers use this to evaluate correctness without re-deriving intent. Set to `"N/A"` only if the change was purely mechanical with no meaningful trade-offs.

- **`test_coverage_notes`** — Describe what the tester agent should verify: new code paths, edge cases introduced, regression risks, and any known untested scenarios left to the tester. Set to `"N/A"` only if the bead touched no executable code paths (e.g., documentation-only changes).

- **`known_limitations`** — Call out constraints, deferred work, or known gaps in the implementation. This includes out-of-scope items deliberately left for follow-up beads and any areas where the implementation is intentionally incomplete. Set to `"N/A"` if the implementation is complete as specified with no known gaps.

Expected outputs:
- Completed or blocked JSON with concise implementation summary.
- Accurate touched files, changed files, risks, and follow-up handoff fields.
- Populated `design_decisions`, `test_coverage_notes`, and `known_limitations` fields in every response.
